title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: We continue our focus on our Perpetual Productivity Improvement initiatives and managing what is within our control.
epigraph.author: Lowe's Companies, Inc., FY2025 Form 10-K MD&A

web_blocks.title: 5.1 Leading Operational KPIs: Separating Housing Macro Drag from Internal Execution

web_blocks.html: Judging Lowe's operating health requires looking past headline sales. Q3 FY2026 revenue jumped +9.3% year-over-year ($22,756 million vs. $20,813 million), largely because FBM and ADG entered the base [2]. Six leading KPIs tell the real story. First, comparable sales turned positive after two down years (-4.7% in FY2023 and -2.7% in FY2024) [1, 2, 24]. Comps reached +0.2% in FY2025 and rose to +1.8% in Q3 FY2026 (+0.3% August, +2.9% September, +2.0% October)—Lowe's sixth straight positive quarter [1, 2, 24]. Management raised FY2026 comp guidance to ~+0.5%, up from flat [2]. Second, comparable retail transactions remain a clear watchpoint. Total transactions fell from 827 million in FY2023 to 801 million in FY2024 and 780 million in FY2025 (-2.8% comp transactions), then slipped another 1.7% in Q3 FY2026 [1, 24]. Higher average tickets ($106.13 in FY2025, +3.0% comp ticket) and Pro/Appliance mix—not recovering DIY traffic—are carrying comps [1, 24].

Third, digital and omnichannel velocity is now Lowe's top organic growth engine. Online sales rose +17.4% year-over-year in Q3 FY2026—the fifth straight double-digit quarter and third straight above 15% [2, 14, 24]. Better mobile conversion, the 3P marketplace, and the 'Mylow' AI assistant drove that pace [2, 14, 24]. Fourth, Pro and Home Services keep beating core DIY. Home Services posted its tenth straight positive comp quarter in Q3 FY2026, while small-Pro accounts grew under MyLowe's Pro Rewards [14, 24]. Fifth, operating margin and ROIC have stepped down from peak levels. GAAP operating margin eased from 13.38% (FY2023) to 12.51% (FY2024), 11.77% (FY2025), and ~11.1% guided for FY2026 (11.5% adjusted, excluding ~40 bps of FBM/ADG amortization) [1, 2]. ROIC moved from 36.4% (FY2023) to 32.0% (FY2024) and 26.1% (FY2025) as $10.1 billion of deal capital entered the base [1, 2]. Sixth, FBM/ADG integration is on track. In November 2026, CFO Brandon Sink noted Lowe's already captured most targeted drywall, steel, and insulation buying savings (extending into 2027), plans ~15 new FBM branches in 2026, and is piloting cross-channel credit [9, 20].

web_blocks.title: 5.2 Structural Operating Leverage & Multi-Year Growth Algorithm

web_blocks.html: To judge Lowe's earnings power across the cycle, use management's operating-leverage rule of thumb. Every 100 basis points of incremental comp sales adds roughly 10 basis points of operating margin [22]. That math explains why margins slid from 13.38% in FY2023 to ~11.1% guided in FY2026 when flat sales met rising store wages [1, 22]. It also shows why profits snap back once existing-home sales move above 4 million annualized units [1, 22]. Beyond macro recovery, Lowe's Perpetual Productivity Improvement (PPI) program targets ~$1 billion in annual cost savings [1, 14]. Those gains come from freight tuning, AI shelf restocking, self-checkout upgrades, and leaner headquarters overhead—including cutting ~600 corporate roles in early 2026 [1, 14]. Over a 3-to-5-year span, 2%–4% retail comps, 15 new FBM branches a year, Pro cross-selling, and mid-2027 buyback resumption support a path back to 12.5%–13.5% operating margins and high-single-digit EPS growth [1, 20, 22].

web_blocks.title: 5.3 Five-Year CEO & CFO Walk-the-Talk Audit (Marvin Ellison & Brandon Sink)
Verified Q3 FY2026 Earnings Call Quotes (CEO Marvin Ellison & CFO Brandon Sink)
paragraphs: CEO Marvin Ellison on omnichannel fulfillment and AI tools (Nov 18, 2026): "50% roughly of orders coming through online are fulfilled out of our stores," and Lowe's Mylow virtual assistant is "answering over million questions a month" to lift digital conversion [28].

CFO Brandon Sink on diesel headwinds and balance-sheet discipline (Nov 18, 2026): On $6-per-gallon diesel costs, Sink noted, "That definitely has been an ongoing pressure that we have spoken to throughout the year," while reiterating capital allocation discipline: "In the next six to 12 months, remain focused on returning to our 2.75x leverage target" [28, 30].

web_blocks.html: A strict governance audit compares promises made against audited results and DEF 14A proxy pay [5]. Since becoming CEO in July 2018 (and Chairman in May 2021), Marvin R. Ellison has built a standout retail turnaround record, joined by CFO Brandon J. Sink since April 2022 [1]. Ellison delivered cleanly on four big promises. First, he exited low-return distractions—Orchard Supply, Mexico, and RONA Canada in February 2023 [18, 19]. Second, he lifted retail operating margins from sub-9% in 2018–2019 to 12%–13.4%, holding 12.16% Retail margins even in trough FY2025 [1, 7]. Third, he grew retail Pro mix from ~19% to ~30% and completed the Market Delivery Model nationwide [13, 23]. Fourth, he protected Lowe's BBB+/Baa1 credit ratings after the 2025 deals [1, 2, 22]. Management paused buybacks ($211 million cash in FY2025 vs. $4,053 million in FY2024) and paid down $2,415 million of debt in 9M FY2026 toward its 2.75x debt-to-EBITDAR goal by mid-2027 [1, 2, 22].

A fair two-sided audit must also flag three real blemishes. First, the long-standing 14%+ operating margin target keeps slipping due to the housing slump and wholesale M&A dilution. In Q3 FY2026 alone, management trimmed FY2026 adjusted margin guidance by 10 basis points to 11.5% [2, 9]. Second, buyback timing was pro-cyclical. Lowe's spent $27.1 billion on buybacks during the FY2021–FY2022 peak ($13.0 billion in FY2021 and $14.1 billion in FY2022), adding debt right before rates jumped [1, 7, 22]. It then borrowed another $7.0 billion in FY2025 to buy FBM and ADG at a reported ~13.4x EBITDA for FBM [1, 7, 22]. Third, the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A) shows Ellison's FY2025 total pay reached $21,581,889—a 578-to-1 ratio versus the $37,371 median U.S. associate [5, 22]. Independent reviewers also noted the Board raised his long-term incentive target after 2023–2025 performance shares failed to vest [5, 22]. Meanwhile, the September 2026 five-executive reshuffle—moving Joe McFarland to lead Pro & Home Services—shows Ellison views FBM/ADG execution as make-or-break [22].

web_blocks.takeaway: Ellison and Sink are elite retail operators with strong delivery on supply chain, portfolio cleanup, and credit discipline. Still, pro-cyclical FY2021–FY2022 buybacks and executive pay alignment warrant ongoing watch.

book_paragraphs: Whenever a company makes a $10 billion acquisition, headline revenue stops telling you the truth about organic health. That is exactly the trap sitting in front of anyone glancing at Lowe's Q3 FY2026 press release, which boasted 9.3% total sales growth to $22.8 billion. Almost all of that headline jump came from adding Foundation Building Materials and Artisan Design Group to the top line. To see whether Lowe's core engine is actually healthy, you and I have to strip away the M&A noise and inspect the operational gauges on the dashboard.

The news on that dashboard is genuinely mixed—strong enough to confirm a resilient franchise, yet soft enough to demand patience. On the positive side, Lowe's just posted its sixth consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales, accelerating to +1.8% in Q3 FY2026, prompting management to nudge full-year comp guidance up to +0.5%. Online sales jumped 17.4%—the fifth straight quarter of double-digit digital growth—while Home Services logged its tenth straight positive quarter and Appliances delivered its best comp performance in five years. In a housing market stuck near multi-decade lows in existing-home sales, grinding out positive comps at all is a real operational achievement.

Yet look one line deeper at retail customer transactions, and you will see why we rate Lowe's KPI health as PASS_WITH_WATCH rather than an unqualified pass. Total retail transactions fell from 827 million in FY2023 to 801 million in FY2024 and 780 million in FY2025, and dipped another 1.7% in Q3 FY2026. Positive comps are being lifted by higher average tickets ($106.13) and commercial baskets rather than bustling DIY aisles. Because store wages rise every year regardless of foot traffic, flat retail sales have steadily compressed consolidated GAAP operating margin from 13.38% in FY2023 down to 11.77% in FY2025 and an expected 11.1% in FY2026.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The 10-Basis-Point Rule of Thumb
book_callouts.text: Management has shared a simple operating-leverage math rule that you should keep in your pocket: every 1% of comparable sales growth adds roughly 10 basis points to Lowe's operating margin. That rule explains why flat comps pinched margins over the last three years—and why even a modest 3% to 4% housing-turnover rebound can quickly restore operating leverage.

book_subsections.title: Grading Marvin Ellison: Operational Master, Pro-Cyclical Capital Allocator
paragraphs: When you and I grade CEO Marvin Ellison and CFO Brandon Sink on a five-year walk-the-talk audit, we have to separate store operations from capital-allocation timing. As a retail operator, Ellison has been exceptional. He kept his word on amputating Canada (selling RONA to Sycamore Partners in 2023), built the Market Delivery Model that turned Appliances into a runaway winner, lifted retail Pro share from 19% to 30%, and committed to roughly $1 billion a year in Perpetual Productivity Improvement savings. Better yet, when he pulled the trigger on $10.1 billion of cash acquisitions in 2025, he immediately hit the brakes on share buybacks and paid down $2.4 billion of debt during the first nine months of FY2026 to protect Lowe's BBB+ and Baa1 investment-grade ratings.

Where an honest analyst must push back is on buyback timing and executive pay governance. Between FY2021 and FY2022, when pandemic stimulus inflated home-improvement profits to peak levels, Lowe's poured $27.1 billion into share repurchases—driving book equity deeply negative and pushing debt higher right before interest rates climbed. Then, when the housing slump arrived and M&A demanded cash, buybacks had to be paused until mid-2027. Meanwhile, the 2026 proxy statement reveals Ellison earned $21.58 million in FY2025—578 times the median associate's $37,371 pay—with the board raising his long-term incentive target even after 2023–2025 performance shares missed their return hurdles. Ellison has earned the benefit of the doubt on store execution, and his September 2026 reshuffle putting veteran operator Joe McFarland in charge of Pro and Home Services shows urgency. Still, you and I should judge management over the next eight quarters by two hard numbers: getting leverage back to 2.75x on schedule, and turning FBM and ADG from zero-margin GAAP diluters into genuine ROIC contributors.

book_subsections.title: Perpetual Productivity, AI Tools, and the Four KPIs That Will Drive the Next Leg
paragraphs: One reason Lowe's has protected double-digit operating margins through three sluggish housing years is a quiet internal engine management calls Perpetual Productivity Improvement, or PPI. Rather than waiting for a macro boom to bail out rising store wages, Ellison's team targets roughly $1 billion in annualized productivity savings every single year. Those savings come from tangible, unglamorous operational upgrades: rolling out modernized front-end self-checkout stations, streamlining overnight freight flow from trailer to shelf, deploying AI-enabled full-shelf replenishment to cut out-of-stocks, and trimming roughly 600 corporate and support roles in early 2026 to keep headquarters lean. On the customer-facing side, Lowe's partnered with OpenAI to launch Mylow—the first generative AI home-improvement shopping assistant among major U.S. chains—alongside Mylow Companion for store associates, helping part-time staff answer complex plumbing or electrical questions without losing a sale.

Yet as a disciplined investor, you and I never take management's AI slides or PPI slogans on faith—we demand proof in the quarterly KPIs. Over the next four to six quarters, four specific leading indicators will tell us whether Lowe's graduates from PASS_WITH_WATCH back to an unqualified PASS. First, watch comparable retail customer transactions: they must stop shrinking (-1.7% in Q3 FY2026) and stabilize flat-to-positive, proving DIY shoppers are returning alongside higher ticket sizes. Second, watch Retail Home Improvement segment operating margin in Note 13 of each Form 10-Q to confirm store-level profitability stays resilient above 12% to 13% despite wage and diesel inflation. Third, watch the 'Other' segment (FBM and ADG) move decisively out of near-zero GAAP operating margins as procurement synergies in drywall, steel, and insulation compound and cross-channel trade credit pilots scale nationwide. Fourth, watch CFO Brandon Sink hit the 2.75x lease-adjusted debt-to-EBITDAR target by mid-2027, reopening the $10.8 billion remaining share-repurchase authorization.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Track the Four Leading Gauges, Not the Headlines
callouts.text: Headline sales growth of 9.3% will fool casual observers during an acquisition year. Keep your eyes locked on comparable retail transactions, Retail segment operating margin, FBM/ADG operating profit ramp, and lease-adjusted leverage—those four gauges tell the unfiltered truth.
